ut-shan-noodles: Fry the sliced shallot in oil until deep gold and set half aside for serving.
Add the garlic, paprika and turmeric and warm them a minute, until fragrant.
Add the minced chicken and fry it, breaking up lumps, until it whitens.
Add the chopped tomatoes and fish sauce and stew twenty-five minutes to a thick paste.
Grind the peanuts to a coarse crumb, keeping a few whole.
Boil the rice noodles, rinse them and divide them between bowls.
Spoon the sauce over the noodles and top with peanuts, fried shallot, pickled greens and coriander.
ut-shan-noodles-nf: Fry the sliced shallot in oil until deep gold and set half aside for serving.
Add the garlic, paprika and turmeric and warm them a minute, until fragrant.
Add the minced chicken and fry it, breaking up lumps, until it whitens.
Add the chopped tomatoes and fish sauce and stew twenty-five minutes to a thick paste.
Grind the toasted sunflower seeds to a coarse crumb, keeping a few whole.
Boil the rice noodles, rinse them and divide them between bowls.
Spoon the sauce over the noodles and top with toasted sunflower seeds, fried shallot, pickled greens and coriander.
ut-ohn-no-khao-swe: Pound the onion, garlic and ginger to a paste and fry it in oil with the turmeric and paprika.
Add the chicken in small pieces and fry it until it whitens all over.
Add a litre of water and the fish sauce and simmer twenty minutes.
Slake the chickpea flour in a cup of cold water until completely smooth and lump-free.
Pour the slaked flour into the broth in a thin stream, whisking without stopping.
Cook ten minutes to thicken, add the coconut milk and warm it five minutes without boiling.
Boil the noodles, divide them between bowls, ladle over the broth and serve with egg, lime and chilli.
ut-ohn-no-khao-swe-gf: Pound the onion, garlic and ginger to a paste and fry it in oil with the turmeric and paprika.
Add the chicken in small pieces and fry it until it whitens all over.
Add a litre of water and the fish sauce and simmer twenty minutes.
Slake the chickpea flour in a cup of cold water until completely smooth and lump-free.
Pour the slaked gram flour (chickpea flour) into the broth in a thin stream, whisking without stopping.
Cook ten minutes to thicken, add the coconut milk and warm it five minutes without boiling.
Boil the rice noodles, divide them between bowls, ladle over the broth and serve with egg, lime and chilli.
ut-num-banh-chok: Poach the fish in salted water for ten minutes, lift it out and pick it by hand, removing every bone.
Pound the lemongrass, galangal, turmeric and lime leaves in a mortar into a kroeung paste.
Work the picked fish into the paste in the mortar, keeping the threads distinguishable.
Warm the fish and spice mixture in a pan for five minutes, then add the prahok and the fish broth.
Add the coconut milk and warm it ten minutes without letting it boil.
Shred all the vegetables fine and pile them on a large platter.
Boil the noodles, rinse them in cold water and serve them cold under the warm curry.
ut-samlor-korko: Toast the rice in a dry pan to a deep gold and grind it to a fine powder.
Pound the lemongrass, galangal, turmeric and garlic into a kroeung paste.
Fry the paste in oil for five minutes, add the prahok and cook two minutes more.
Add the pork and brown it, then pour in a litre and a half of water.
Cook twenty minutes, then add the pumpkin, papaya and aubergine.
Add the rice powder, first stirred into a ladle of the broth, and cook ten minutes.
Add the beans and moringa leaves for the last five minutes and adjust with fish sauce and palm sugar.
ut-torta-frita: Mix the flour with the salt and baking powder in a large bowl.
Melt the lard and stir it into the hot water until even.
Pour the liquid into the flour and work it with a spoon until it cools enough to handle.
Knead by hand for ten minutes to a smooth elastic dough.
Cover it and rest it twenty minutes at room temperature.
Divide it into eight, roll each into a half-centimetre round and cut a slit in the centre.
Fry at 180 °C for a minute and a half a side and serve with sugar or dulce de leche.
ut-torta-frita-gf: Mix the gluten-free flour with the salt and baking powder in a large bowl.
Melt the lard and stir it into the hot water until even.
Pour the liquid into the gluten-free flour and work it with a spoon until it cools enough to handle.
Knead by hand for ten minutes to a smooth elastic dough.
Cover it and rest it twenty minutes at room temperature.
Divide it into eight, roll each into a half-centimetre round and cut a slit in the centre.
Fry at 180 °C for a minute and a half a side and serve with sugar or dulce de leche.
ut-buseca: Rinse the tripe several times, rub it with salt and rinse it again until completely clean.
Boil the tripe in water with half the vinegar for ten minutes and throw away that first water.
Cover it with fresh water and the bay and simmer three hours, until completely tender.
Boil the beans separately until soft, an hour and a quarter, and set them aside with their liquid.
Fry the pancetta and the sliced chorizo, add the onion, carrot and celery and sweat them ten minutes.
Stir in the paprika and tomatoes, add the sliced tripe with some of its broth and the potato.
Cook twenty-five minutes, stir in the beans with their liquid, season and warm it ten more.
ut-kak-ik: Simmer the turkey with an onion in three litres of water for ninety minutes, skimming.
Seed the chillies and char them on a dry pan for ten seconds a side.
Char the tomatoes, tomatillos, onion and garlic on the same pan until blackened in patches.
Toast the coriander, achiote and mace on a dry pan until fragrant.
Blend everything with two ladles of the broth to a smooth red mass.
Strain the mass through a sieve into the pot with the turkey and cook twenty-five minutes.
Add the samat and mint for the last five minutes and serve with corn tamalitos.
ut-rellenitos: Boil the plantains in their skins for twenty minutes, until completely soft.
Peel them hot and mash them into a smooth purée with a pinch of salt and the flour.
Chill the purée for half an hour; warm, it will not hold as balls.
Mash the cooked beans and reduce them with the sugar, cinnamon and cloves to a thick paste.
Stir the chocolate into the hot bean paste and cool it completely.
Flatten a piece of purée on your palm, add the bean filling and seal it into a firm ball.
Fry at 170 °C for three minutes, to a browned crust, and serve with icing sugar and soured cream.
ut-rellenitos-gf: Boil the plantains in their skins for twenty minutes, until completely soft.
Peel them hot and mash them into a smooth purée with a pinch of salt and the gluten-free flour.
Chill the purée for half an hour; warm, it will not hold as balls.
Mash the cooked beans and reduce them with the sugar, cinnamon and cloves to a thick paste.
Stir the chocolate into the hot bean paste and cool it completely.
Flatten a piece of purée on your palm, add the bean filling and seal it into a firm ball.
Fry at 170 °C for three minutes, to a browned crust, and serve with icing sugar and soured cream.
ut-pollo-guisado-dominicano: Wash the chicken with lime juice, rub it with oregano, garlic, salt and pepper and leave it an hour.
Melt the sugar in the oil over medium heat to a dark amber, without stirring with a spoon.
Put the chicken pieces into the caramel and brown them on all sides.
Add the onion, pepper and tomato paste and cook five minutes, stirring.
Add a cup of water, cover and stew twenty-five minutes on a low heat.
Add the potato in large pieces and stew twenty minutes more, until tender.
Stir in the olives and coriander, reduce the sauce to a coating consistency and serve with white rice.
ut-habichuelas-con-dulce: Boil the soaked beans in fresh water for an hour, until completely soft.
Blend the beans with some of their liquid to a smooth mass.
Press the mass through a sieve with a spoon and discard the skins left behind.
Return it to the heat and add the coconut and evaporated milk, cinnamon, cloves and sugar.
Cook twenty minutes on a low heat, stirring so it does not catch.
Add the sweet potato in pieces and the raisins and cook twenty minutes more, until the potato is tender.
Stir in the vanilla, butter and a pinch of salt, chill it and serve it cold with gluten-free biscuits.
ut-trinidad-roti: Knead a soft dough from the flour, baking powder, salt and warm water, working it ten minutes.
Cover it and rest it an hour; the dough should become pliable and stop springing back.
Marinate the chicken with the curry powder, garlic, thyme and salt and stew it with the potato for forty minutes.
Divide the dough into six balls, roll each one thin and brush it with oil.
Roll the round into a rope, coil it into a spiral and let it rest twenty minutes.
Roll the spirals out into rounds again and cook them on a dry pan a minute and a half a side, brushing with ghee.
Move the bread onto a board and beat it into soft rags with two spatulas. Serve with the curry.
ut-trinidad-roti-gf: Knead a soft dough from the gluten-free flour, baking powder, salt and warm water, working it ten minutes.
Cover it and rest it an hour; the dough should become pliable and stop springing back.
Marinate the chicken with the curry powder, garlic, thyme and salt and stew it with the potato for forty minutes.
Divide the dough into six balls, roll each one thin and brush it with oil.
Roll the round into a rope, coil it into a spiral and let it rest twenty minutes.
Roll the spirals out into rounds again and cook them on a dry pan a minute and a half a side, brushing with ghee.
Move the gluten-free bread onto a board and beat it into soft rags with two spatulas. Serve with the curry.
ut-pelau: Marinate the chicken in the green seasoning, ketchup, salt and pepper for at least an hour.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and add the sugar, without stirring it with a spoon.
Wait until the sugar darkens almost to black and starts to smoke, and put the chicken in at once.
Fry the chicken, turning it in the caramel, until every piece is dark brown.
Add the onion, carrot, pumpkin and pigeon peas and warm them five minutes.
Add the rinsed rice, pour in the coconut milk and water to a finger above and drop in the whole chilli.
Cover and cook twenty-five minutes on a low heat without opening it. Serve with coleslaw.
ut-hallaca: Warm the annatto seeds in the lard for five minutes and strain it; the coloured fat goes into both dough and guiso.
Fry the onion and pepper in the annatto fat, add all three meats and brown them.
Add the wine and stock and stew an hour, until the meat is tender and the sauce thick.
Cool the guiso completely, ideally leaving it overnight in the fridge.
Knead a dough from the masarepa, warm stock, annatto fat and salt until pliable.
Warm the banana leaves, spread a disc of dough on each and add guiso, olives, raisins and capers.
Wrap in two leaves, tie them crosswise with string and boil them for an hour and twenty.
ut-asado-negro: Pierce the meat in several places with a knife, rub it with salt, pepper and garlic and leave it an hour.
Melt the panela in oil in a heavy pot until nearly black, without stirring it with a spoon.
Lower the beef into the caramel and sear it on all sides to a black crust, about fifteen minutes.
Lift out the meat and fry the onion, pepper, carrot and leek in the same fat until soft.
Return the meat, add the tomatoes, wine, Worcestershire sauce and bay, and add water to half its height.
Braise covered for four hours on the lowest heat, turning the joint every hour.
Lift out the meat, strain the sauce, reduce it by half and slice the beef across the grain.
ut-asado-negro-gf: Pierce the meat in several places with a knife, rub it with salt, pepper and garlic and leave it an hour.
Melt the panela in oil in a heavy pot until nearly black, without stirring it with a spoon.
Lower the beef into the caramel and sear it on all sides to a black crust, about fifteen minutes.
Lift out the meat and fry the onion, pepper, carrot and leek in the same fat until soft.
Return the meat, add the tomatoes, wine, tamari and bay, and add water to half its height.
Braise covered for four hours on the lowest heat, turning the joint every hour.
Lift out the meat, strain the sauce, reduce it by half and slice the beef across the grain.
ut-pique-macho: Cut the potatoes into thick batons and soak them in cold water for twenty minutes.
Dry the potatoes and fry them twice: at 150 °C until soft, then at 190 °C until crisp.
Sear the diced beef over a high flame in batches for two minutes each and set it aside.
Fry the sliced sausages until browned and add the onion and pepper for five minutes.
Return the meat to the pan, add the tomatoes and mustard and warm it three minutes.
Fry the eggs with runny yolks and cut the locoto into thin rings.
Pile the chips on a platter, top with the meat and vegetables, the eggs and the locoto rings, and drizzle with mayonnaise and ketchup.
ut-api-morado: Soak the purple corn in cold water overnight, keeping that water in the morning.
Grind the corn with its water in a blender to an even purple liquid.
Strain it through a fine sieve, pressing the pulp, and strain it a second time.
Add the remaining water, the cinnamon, cloves and orange peel.
Cook over medium heat for forty minutes, stirring with a wooden spoon, until it thickens.
Add the sugar and lemon juice and cook five minutes more.
Remove the spices and serve it hot in mugs, with a fried cheese gluten-free pastry.
ut-ceviche-ecuatoriano: Peel the prawns, boil the shells in a litre of water for twenty minutes and strain the broth.
Poach the prawns in that broth for exactly two minutes and drop them straight into iced water.
Chill the broth completely; it becomes the base of the dressing.
Slice the red onion thin, rinse it in cold water and cure it in lime juice with salt.
Blend two tomatoes to a purée and mix it with the ketchup, mustard, orange juice and the cold broth.
Combine the prawns, cured onion, chopped tomatoes and the dressing.
Chill it an hour, stir in the coriander and serve with popcorn and plantain crisps.
ut-fanesca: Soak the cod for a day with four changes of water and poach it in milk for twenty minutes.
Boil the beans, lupini, broad beans, lentils and peas separately until soft.
Grind the peanuts with milk to a smooth mass; it is the soup's thickener.
Fry the onion in annatto oil, add the pumpkin and courgette and stew twenty minutes.
Blend the pumpkin and courgette and return them to the pot with the cod's milk.
Stir in all the cooked pulses, the rice, corn and peanut mass and cook thirty minutes.
Add the cream, cheese and pieces of cod, and serve with halved eggs and fried plantain.
ut-fanesca-nf: Soak the cod for a day with four changes of water and poach it in milk for twenty minutes.
Boil the beans, lupini, broad beans, lentils and peas separately until soft.
Grind the toasted sunflower seeds with milk to a smooth mass; it is the soup's thickener.
Fry the onion in annatto oil, add the pumpkin and courgette and stew twenty minutes.
Blend the pumpkin and courgette and return them to the pot with the cod's milk.
Stir in all the cooked pulses, the rice, corn and toasted sunflower seeds mass and cook thirty minutes.
Add the cream, cheese and pieces of cod, and serve with halved eggs and fried plantain.
ut-carimanola: Peel the cassava, strip the woody core and boil it in salted water until completely soft.
Mash the cassava hot and work it with the egg and salt into a pliable dough.
Fry the onion, pepper and garlic, add the mince, cumin and tomato paste and cook it through.
Stir the culantro into the filling and cool it completely.
Take a lump of dough with wet hands, flatten it on your palm and put the filling in the centre.
Seal it and draw it into a torpedo with pointed ends.
Fry at 175 °C for four minutes, to a deep golden crust, and serve them hot.
ut-arroz-con-coco: Pour the coconut milk into a heavy pot and cook it over medium heat, stirring.
Keep cooking until the milk separates into oil and brown solids.
The moment the solids turn deep brown, add the water at once to stop the caramelisation.
Add the sugar, salt and raisins and bring it to the boil.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and add it to the pot in an even layer.
Cook uncovered over medium heat until the liquid falls to the level of the rice.
Cover it, drop the heat to its lowest and hold it twenty minutes without opening it once.
ut-kugelis: Render the bacon to crackling, add the chopped onion and fry it golden.
Grate the potatoes finely and squeeze them lightly, collecting the liquid in a bowl.
Let the liquid stand ten minutes, pour off the water and stir the settled starch back in.
Add the hot milk and the hot fat with the onion and crackling, stirring quickly.
Work in the eggs, salt, pepper and marjoram to an even thick mass.
Pour it into a greased dish in a four-centimetre layer and level it.
Bake at 180 °C for an hour and a half, to a deep golden crust, and rest it twenty minutes.
ut-sakotis: Separate the whites from the yolks and whip the whites with half the sugar to firm peaks.
Beat the softened butter with the remaining sugar until pale, about eight minutes.
Add the yolks one at a time, still beating, then work in the soured cream, vanilla and zest.
Sift the flour with the starch and salt and fold it in with a spatula in three additions.
Fold in the whipped whites gently so the mixture does not collapse; the batter has to stay airy.
Heat the oven to 190 °C and pour the first thin layer onto a greased spit or into a tin.
Bake each layer three minutes to a golden colour and pour the next, until the batter runs out.
ut-sakotis-gf: Separate the whites from the yolks and whip the whites with half the sugar to firm peaks.
Beat the softened butter with the remaining sugar until pale, about eight minutes.
Add the yolks one at a time, still beating, then work in the soured cream, vanilla and zest.
Sift the gluten-free flour with the starch and salt and fold it in with a spatula in three additions.
Fold in the whipped whites gently so the mixture does not collapse; the batter has to stay airy.
Heat the oven to 190 °C and pour the first thin layer onto a greased spit or into a tin.
Bake each layer three minutes to a golden colour and pour the next, until the batter runs out.
ut-sklandrausis: Knead a dough from the rye flour, warm water, melted butter and salt and rest it half an hour.
Boil the potatoes and carrots separately until completely soft.
Mash the potatoes with soured cream, an egg, caraway and salt into a smooth purée.
Mash the carrots with soured cream, an egg, sugar and cinnamon into a separate purée.
Roll the dough thin, cut rounds and shape rims with your fingers, folding the edges up.
Spread the potato purée as the first layer and the carrot over it, levelling with a spoon.
Bake at 200 °C for twenty-five minutes and dust them with cinnamon while still hot.
ut-skabu-putra: Rinse the barley and soak it in cold water for two hours.
Boil the barley in a litre and a half of water for an hour, until it collapses entirely.
Salt the porridge and cool it completely, stirring so no skin forms.
Work the curdled milk into the cold porridge gradually, to the consistency of a thick soup.
Leave it four hours somewhere cold so the sourness develops and evens out.
Boil the potatoes in their skins and serve them hot alongside.
Ladle it into bowls, add soured cream and scatter with spring onion and dill.
ut-skabu-putra-gf: Rinse the brown rice and soak it in cold water for two hours.
Boil the brown rice in a litre and a half of water for an hour, until it collapses entirely.
Salt the porridge and cool it completely, stirring so no skin forms.
Work the curdled milk into the cold porridge gradually, to the consistency of a thick soup.
Leave it four hours somewhere cold so the sourness develops and evens out.
Boil the potatoes in their skins and serve them hot alongside.
Ladle it into bowls, add soured cream and scatter with spring onion and dill.
ut-verivorst: Boil the barley in salted water for forty minutes, to half done, and drain it.
Render the pork fat to crackling, add the onion and fry it golden.
Cool both the barley and the fat with onion completely, or the blood sets when they meet.
Strain the blood through a sieve and mix it with the barley, fat, marjoram, allspice and salt.
Rinse the casings and fill them two-thirds full, leaving room for the barley to swell.
Tie the sausages every twenty centimetres and prick them in several places with a needle.
Bake at 180 °C for forty-five minutes, dotted with butter, and serve with lingonberry jam.
ut-verivorst-gf: Boil the brown rice in salted water for forty minutes, to half done, and drain it.
Render the pork fat to crackling, add the onion and fry it golden.
Cool both the brown rice and the fat with onion completely, or the blood sets when they meet.
Strain the blood through a sieve and mix it with the brown rice, fat, marjoram, allspice and salt.
Rinse the casings and fill them two-thirds full, leaving room for the brown rice to swell.
Tie the sausages every twenty centimetres and prick them in several places with a needle.
Bake at 180 °C for forty-five minutes, dotted with butter, and serve with lingonberry jam.
ut-kohuke: Push the curd through a fine sieve twice, until not a single grain remains.
Beat the softened butter with the icing sugar, vanilla and salt until fluffy.
Combine the curd with the butter mixture and work in the cream to the body of a firm cream.
Fold in the raisins and shape twelve finger-sized bars.
Lay the bars on parchment and freeze them two hours, until solid.
Melt the chocolate with the coconut oil over a water bath until smooth and cool it to lukewarm.
Dip the frozen bars on two forks, let them drain and set them on parchment to harden.
ut-kolduny: Soak the dried mushrooms in warm water for twenty minutes and chop them fine.
Fry two onions with the mince and mushrooms, add the marjoram, salt and pepper and cool it completely.
Grate the potatoes and the remaining onion finely into one bowl.
Let the mass stand three minutes and pour off the water that gathers, leaving the sediment.
Work in the egg and season the potato mass.
Put a spoon of the mass on your palm, add filling and cover it with a second spoon, sealing the edges.
Fry them three minutes a side, move them to a pan, pour over the soured cream and stew fifteen minutes.
ut-kholodnik: Boil the beetroot until tender with a spoon of vinegar so it keeps its colour, and cool it completely.
Cook the sorrel in a little water for five minutes, until it darkens, and cool it.
Grate the cooled beetroot coarsely and cut the cucumbers into matchsticks.
Mix the beetroot, the sorrel with its liquid, the cucumber and herbs with the soured cream and salt it.
Add the cold kefir and stir to an even pink.
Chill it an hour so the soup infuses and turns genuinely cold.
Boil the potatoes and serve them hot on a separate plate, with halved eggs in the soup.
ut-zemiakove-placky: Grate the potatoes finely and squeeze them lightly, leaving some moisture in.
Crush the garlic with salt into a paste and work it into the potato mass.
Add the egg, milk, marjoram, pepper and flour and stir to a loose batter.
Heat the oil over medium and pour in a ladle of batter, spreading it very thin.
Fry three minutes a side, to a deep golden crisp crust.
Drain them on a rack rather than paper and serve them at once.
ut-zemiakove-placky-gf: Grate the potatoes finely and squeeze them lightly, leaving some moisture in.
Crush the garlic with salt into a paste and work it into the potato mass.
Add the egg, milk, marjoram, pepper and gluten-free flour and stir to a loose batter.
Heat the oil over medium and pour in a ladle of batter, spreading it very thin.
Fry three minutes a side, to a deep golden crisp crust.
Drain them on a rack rather than paper and serve them at once.
ut-sladke-buchty: Dissolve the yeast with a spoon of sugar in the warm milk and leave it fifteen minutes, until it foams.
Knead a dough from the flour, sponge, yolks, remaining sugar, zest, salt and half the butter.
Let it rise somewhere warm for an hour, until doubled.
Divide it into twelve balls and flatten each into a disc on your palm.
Put a spoon of jam or curd in each, seal the seam and turn them seam down.
Dip each bun in melted butter and pack them touching in a tin.
Prove them forty minutes, bake at 180 °C for thirty-five minutes and dust them with icing sugar.
ut-struklji: Knead a soft dough from the flour, warm water, oil and salt and work it fifteen minutes.
Cover it with a warmed bowl and rest it forty minutes; the dough has to turn pliable.
Work the curd with the eggs, soured cream, sugar and raisins until even.
Stretch the dough by hand on a cloth until translucent, as for strudel.
Spread the filling over the sheet, leaving the edges clear, and roll it up using the cloth.
Wrap the roll loosely in a clean cloth, tie the ends and lower it into boiling salted water.
Boil it forty minutes, unwrap it, cut it into rounds and fry them in butter with the breadcrumbs.
ut-struklji-gf: Knead a soft dough from the gluten-free flour, warm water, oil and salt and work it fifteen minutes.
Cover it with a warmed bowl and rest it forty minutes; the dough has to turn pliable.
Work the curd with the eggs, soured cream, sugar and raisins until even.
Stretch the dough by hand on a cloth until translucent, as for strudel.
Spread the filling over the sheet, leaving the edges clear, and roll it up using the cloth.
Wrap the roll loosely in a clean cloth, tie the ends and lower it into boiling salted water.
Boil it forty minutes, unwrap it, cut it into rounds and fry them in butter with the gluten-free breadcrumbs.
ut-kranjska-klobasa: Dice the pork and fat and chill them to just above freezing.
Put the meat through the coarse plate of a mincer and the fat through the medium one.
Work in the curing salt, crushed garlic, pepper and iced water and knead the mixture until tacky.
Leave the mixture in the fridge for a day so the salt distributes and the colour sets.
Fill the casings tightly but without air pockets and tie them in twenty-centimetre pairs.
Air-dry the sausages two hours and cold-smoke them if you can.
Lower them into water at 75 °C and hold them twenty-five minutes without letting it boil. Serve with horseradish and mustard.
ut-begova-corba: Simmer the chicken and veal with the onion, carrot and celeriac for an hour, skimming.
Lift out the meat, strain the broth and pull the chicken into fine threads.
Rinse the okra under cold water and pat it dry without trimming the caps.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook it two minutes without letting it colour.
Pour the broth into the roux, add the okra and cook fifteen minutes.
Whisk the yolks with the soured cream and ladle in hot broth, stirring without stopping.
Take the pot off the heat, pour in the mixture, return the meat and warm it through without boiling. Add lemon and parsley.
ut-begova-corba-gf: Simmer the chicken and veal with the onion, carrot and celeriac for an hour, skimming.
Lift out the meat, strain the broth and pull the chicken into fine threads.
Rinse the okra under cold water and pat it dry without trimming the caps.
Melt the butter, stir in the gluten-free flour and cook it two minutes without letting it colour.
Pour the broth into the roux, add the okra and cook fifteen minutes.
Whisk the yolks with the soured cream and ladle in hot broth, stirring without stopping.
Take the pot off the heat, pour in the mixture, return the meat and warm it through without boiling. Add lemon and parsley.
ut-tufahije: Peel the apples and core them without going through, so each forms a cup.
Make a syrup of water, sugar, lemon juice and cinnamon, bringing it to the boil.
Lower the apples into the syrup and poach them twenty minutes on a low heat, turning them.
Lift the apples out with a slotted spoon and cool them completely, keeping the syrup.
Mix the ground walnuts with three spoons of the syrup into a pliable mass.
Fill the apples with the walnut mass, mounded, and set them in dishes.
Spoon over the remaining syrup and top with whipped cream and a walnut half.
ut-tufahije-nf: Peel the apples and core them without going through, so each forms a cup.
Make a syrup of water, sugar, lemon juice and cinnamon, bringing it to the boil.
Lower the apples into the syrup and poach them twenty minutes on a low heat, turning them.
Lift the apples out with a slotted spoon and cool them completely, keeping the syrup.
Mix the ground pumpkin seeds with three spoons of the syrup into a pliable mass.
Fill the apples with the pumpkin seeds mass, mounded, and set them in dishes.
Spoon over the remaining syrup and top with whipped cream and a pumpkin seeds half.
ut-ohridska-pastrmka: Rinse the trout, pat them dry and cut two slashes on each side.
Rub the fish with salt, pepper, paprika and olive oil inside and out.
Tuck lemon slices, garlic, parsley and thyme into each cavity.
Slice the potatoes thin and lay them overlapping on an oiled tray.
Set the fish on the potatoes and pour over the wine and the remaining oil.
Bake at 200 °C for twenty-five minutes, until the skin colours.
Test at the spine and serve straight from the tray with a wedge of lemon.
ut-pastrmajlija: Dice the pork into centimetre cubes, salt it generously and leave it two hours in the cold.
Dissolve the yeast in the warm water and leave it ten minutes, until it foams.
Knead a soft dough from the flour, sponge, oil and salt and work it ten minutes.
Let it rise an hour somewhere warm, until doubled.
Divide the dough into four and stretch each into an oval thirty centimetres long.
Fold the edges in to make a rim and spread the meat with paprika over the whole surface.
Bake at 250 °C for twenty minutes, crack an egg on top and give it five more.
ut-olla-de-carne: Cover the shank with cold water, bring it to the boil and skim it thoroughly.
Add the onion, pepper and salt and simmer two hours, until the meat is tender.
Cut the cassava into large pieces, removing the woody core, and add it to the broth.
Twenty minutes later add the corn on the cob and the carrots.
Twenty minutes after that add the potatoes and squash in large pieces.
The plantain goes in last and cooks ten minutes, no longer.
Lift the solids out onto a platter, ladle the broth into cups and serve with rice, coriander and lime.
ut-chorreadas: Cut the kernels from the cobs with a knife, running the blade down the core.
Grind the kernels in a blender in short pulses to a grainy mass.
Work in the egg, sugar, salt and corn flour to the consistency of thick cream.
Heat a pan with butter over medium until it just wisps.
Pour in a ladle of batter and spread it into a fifteen-centimetre round.
Fry three minutes a side, to golden patches and a springy centre.
Serve them hot with natilla and a slice of fresh cheese.
ut-montucas: Strip the husks from the cobs whole and rinse them in warm water.
Cut off the kernels and grind them in a blender with the juice they release.
Beat the lard with salt and sugar and work in the corn mass until even.
Simmer the chicken until tender, pull it into threads and keep the broth.
Fry the onion, pepper and tomatoes with the annatto and add the chicken, olives and capers.
Spoon dough onto a husk, add filling, fold it over and tuck the ends under.
Stand the parcels upright in a pot and steam them an hour and a quarter.
ut-pastelitos-hondurenos: Fry the mince with the onion and annatto, add the finely diced potato and stew until soft.
Season the filling and cool it completely.
Shred the cabbage finely and pickle it in vinegar with salt for half an hour.
Mix the masa with warm water and salt to a pliable dough that does not stick to your hands.
Press a ball of dough between two sheets of film into a thin round.
Put a spoon of filling on one half, fold it over and seal the edge with a fork.
Deep-fry at 180 °C for three minutes a side and serve with the cabbage and sauce.
ut-vigoron: Shred the cabbage finely and mix it with the tomatoes, onion, vinegar, lime juice and salt.
Leave the curtido to pickle at least an hour, stirring it now and then.
Cut the pork skin into squares, salt it and leave it twenty minutes.
Render the skin in its own fat over a low heat for forty minutes.
Raise the heat and fry ten minutes more, until the crackling puffs and turns crisp.
Boil the cassava in salted water until tender, having cut out the woody core.
Lay the cassava on a banana leaf, the curtido over it and the crackling on top, with the chilli.
ut-indio-viejo: Simmer the brisket with an onion and salt for an hour and a half, until fully tender.
Lift out the meat, keep the broth and pull the beef into fine threads by hand.
Fry the onion, garlic, pepper and tomatoes with the annatto to a thick base.
Slake the masa in cold broth until smooth, without a single lump.
Add the shredded meat to the vegetable base and warm it five minutes.
Pour in the slaked masa in a thin stream, stirring constantly, and cook twenty minutes.
Add the orange juice, stir in the chopped mint and serve it with rice.
ut-vori-vori: Brown the chicken pieces with the annatto on every side.
Add the onion, pepper, tomatoes and carrot and stew until the vegetables soften.
Pour in two litres of water, salt it and simmer forty minutes over a low heat.
Mix the corn flour with the grated cheese, egg, oregano and a pinch of salt.
Add a couple of spoons of hot broth and work it into a firm dough that holds its shape.
Roll walnut-sized balls, compacting each between your palms.
Drop the balls into the boiling broth, leave them five minutes unstirred and cook twenty. Scatter with parsley.
ut-mbeju: Mix the cassava starch with the corn flour and salt in a wide bowl.
Rub the soft fat into the dry mix with your fingers until it looks like damp sand.
Work in the grated cheese, still rubbing the mixture by hand.
Add the milk a spoon at a time, until the crumb just holds when squeezed in your fist.
Heat a dry pan over medium without adding a drop of oil.
Tip in a centimetre of crumb and press it down with a spatula across the whole surface.
Cook it five minutes, flip it with a plate and colour the second side.
ut-musakhan: Rub the chicken with salt, pepper, allspice, cardamom and cinnamon and leave it half an hour.
Slice the onions into thin half-moons; a kilo and a half takes about twenty minutes.
Stew the onions in the olive oil over a low heat for forty minutes, until translucent and sweet.
Stir two-thirds of the sumac and salt into the onions and give them five more minutes.
Brown the chicken and roast it at 200 °C for twenty-five minutes.
Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan until golden, watching that they do not scorch.
Lay down the bread, the onions on it, the chicken on top, spoon over the pan oil and scatter with sumac and nuts.
ut-galayet-bandora: Cut the tomatoes into large wedges, skins and seeds left in.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pan and soften the onion in it.
Add the crushed garlic and the whole green chillies and warm them a minute.
Tip in the tomatoes, salt them and stew over a medium heat, stirring now and then.
Crush the tomatoes with a spoon once the skins start to lift from the flesh.
Reduce it fifteen minutes more, until the oil rises at the edges as a separate layer.
Scatter with dried mint and serve it in the pan with gluten-free flatbread.
ut-omani-halwa: Slake the starch in half the cold water until completely smooth, with no lumps.
Boil a syrup from the sugar and the remaining water and bring it to a rolling boil.
Pour the starch mixture into the boiling syrup in a thin stream, stirring without stopping.
Steep the saffron in a spoon of hot water and add it to the mass with the cardamom.
Stir over a low heat for an hour and a half, adding the ghee a little at a time.
Work in the honey, rosewater and toasted cashews once the mass starts pulling from the sides.
Spread it in a tin in a three-centimetre layer, level it and cool it six hours.
ut-omani-halwa-nf: Slake the starch in half the cold water until completely smooth, with no lumps.
Boil a syrup from the sugar and the remaining water and bring it to a rolling boil.
Pour the starch mixture into the boiling syrup in a thin stream, stirring without stopping.
Steep the saffron in a spoon of hot water and add it to the mass with the cardamom.
Stir over a low heat for an hour and a half, adding the ghee a little at a time.
Work in the honey, rosewater and toasted sunflower seeds once the mass starts pulling from the sides.
Spread it in a tin in a three-centimetre layer, level it and cool it six hours.
ut-maqdeed: Cut the lamb into two-finger strips along the grain.
Rub the strips all over with salt and turmeric, sparing neither.
Hang the meat in shade with a draught and dry it three to five days, until fully hard.
Soak the dried meat in cold water for two hours, changing the water once.
Boil the meat forty minutes, until it softens and starts to come apart in threads.
Fry the onion with the garlic, cumin and chilli in ghee until golden.
Add the shredded meat and fry ten minutes more, to browned edges. Serve it with rice.
ut-zurbian: Marinate the lamb in yoghurt with the hawaij and salt for two hours.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and soak it thirty minutes.
Fry the onion in ghee to a deep gold and set half of it aside.
Brown the meat with the remaining onion, add the tomatoes and cardamom and stew an hour.
Fry the potato rounds to a golden crust in a separate pan.
Boil the rice in salted water for seven minutes, to half done, and drain it.
Layer the meat, rice, potato and raisins, streak the saffron over and bake it covered for thirty minutes.
ut-fahsa: Cover the ground fenugreek with cold water and leave it six hours, changing the water twice.
Simmer the lamb with the onion and salt for an hour and a half, keeping the broth.
Break the meat into small pieces and return it to the strained broth.
Pound the garlic, chilli and coriander into a sahawiq paste in a mortar.
Add the tomatoes, hawaij and half the paste to the stew and reduce it to a thick body.
Drain the fenugreek and whip it with a spoon of cold water into a white froth.
Ladle the stew into scorching bowls, spoon the froth over and serve it boiling with gluten-free flatbread.
ut-kuwaiti-jireesh: Rinse the cracked wheat and soak it in cold water for an hour.
Fry two of the onions in ghee until soft and add the baharat.
Brown the chicken with the onion and add the tomatoes, tomato paste, cinnamon and pierced dried lime.
Pour in two litres of water, salt it and cook forty minutes, until the chicken is tender.
Lift out the chicken, tip the wheat into the broth and cook it an hour over a low heat.
Mash the porridge until the grain breaks down into a uniform mass.
Fry the remaining onion to deep brown, plate the porridge with the chicken and pour the onion and its butter over.
ut-kuwaiti-jireesh-gf: Rinse the quinoa and soak it in cold water for an hour.
Fry two of the onions in ghee until soft and add the baharat.
Brown the chicken with the onion and add the tomatoes, tomato paste, cinnamon and pierced dried lime.
Pour in two litres of water, salt it and cook forty minutes, until the chicken is tender.
Lift out the chicken, tip the quinoa into the broth and cook it an hour over a low heat.
Mash the porridge until the grain breaks down into a uniform mass.
Fry the remaining onion to deep brown, plate the porridge with the chicken and pour the onion and its butter over.
ut-kuwaiti-darabeel: Dissolve the yeast with the sugar in the warm milk and leave it ten minutes, until it foams.
Steep the saffron in a spoon of hot water and knead a dough with the flour, egg, half the butter and cardamom.
Let the dough rise somewhere warm for an hour, until doubled.
Warm the date paste with the remaining butter and cardamom until soft.
Roll the dough into a rectangle half a centimetre thick and spread the date paste over it.
Roll it up tight and cut it into two-centimetre rounds.
Set them cut side up, prove them twenty minutes and bake at 180 °C for twenty-five minutes.
ut-rechta: Knead a stiff dough from the flour, water, a spoon of oil and salt and work it fifteen minutes.
Roll the dough into a thin sheet and cut it into two-millimetre noodles.
Spread the noodles on a cloth, dust them with flour and dry them twenty minutes.
Simmer the chicken with the onion, chickpeas, cinnamon and white pepper in two litres of water for forty minutes.
Add the turnip in wedges and cook twenty minutes more, until tender.
Steam the noodles over the broth fifteen minutes, take them off, sprinkle with oil and toss them.
Repeat the steaming twice more, mound the noodles, top with the chicken and turnip and ladle broth over.
ut-rechta-gf: Knead a stiff dough from the gluten-free flour, water, a spoon of oil and salt and work it fifteen minutes.
Roll the dough into a thin sheet and cut it into two-millimetre rice noodles.
Spread the rice noodles on a cloth, dust them with gluten-free flour and dry them twenty minutes.
Simmer the chicken with the onion, chickpeas, cinnamon and white pepper in two litres of water for forty minutes.
Add the turnip in wedges and cook twenty minutes more, until tender.
Steam the rice noodles over the broth fifteen minutes, take them off, sprinkle with oil and toss them.
Repeat the steaming twice more, mound the rice noodles, top with the chicken and turnip and ladle broth over.
ut-makroud: Rub the semolina with the olive oil and salt by hand until it is damp all through.
Leave the mixture half an hour so the grain takes up the oil and swells.
Add the warm water with the orange blossom water a little at a time, gathering the dough without kneading.
Steam the dates soft and pound them with the cinnamon and zest into a smooth paste.
Roll the dough into a strip, lay a rope of date paste down the centre and close the edges over it.
Press the strip flat and cut it on the diagonal into four-centimetre diamonds.
Deep-fry at 170 °C until golden and drop them hot into cold honey for five minutes.
ut-gurasa: Dissolve the yeast with the sugar in the warm water and leave it ten minutes, until it foams.
Whisk in the flour and salt to a smooth, loose batter without lumps.
Add the oil and beat another minute, until the batter goes glossy.
Cover it and leave it warm for an hour, until bubbles break the surface.
Heat a dry pan over medium and pour in a ladle of batter.
Cover it and cook five minutes, until the top sets and turns matt.
Lift it out without turning it and stack the breads under a cloth.
ut-salata-aswad: Dice the aubergines, salt them and leave them twenty minutes to draw out the bitterness.
Pat the cubes dry with paper; wet ones spit in the oil.
Fry the aubergine in batches to a dark brown crust and drain it on paper.
Pound the garlic with salt into a paste in a mortar.
Let the peanut butter down with lemon juice, the garlic and water to the body of soured cream.
Chop the tomatoes, onion and chilli fine and mix them with the cooled aubergine.
Pour over the peanut dressing, toss it and let it stand fifteen minutes.
ut-salata-aswad-nf: Dice the aubergines, salt them and leave them twenty minutes to draw out the bitterness.
Pat the cubes dry with paper; wet ones spit in the oil.
Fry the aubergine in batches to a dark brown crust and drain it on paper.
Pound the garlic with salt into a paste in a mortar.
Let the sunflower seed butter down with lemon juice, the garlic and water to the body of soured cream.
Chop the tomatoes, onion and chilli fine and mix them with the cooled aubergine.
Pour over the sunflower seed dressing, toss it and let it stand fifteen minutes.
ut-mchuzi-wa-samaki: Rub the fish steaks with salt and half the curry powder and leave them fifteen minutes.
Fry the fish two minutes a side to a crust and lift it onto a plate.
Soften the onion in the same pan and add the garlic and ginger.
Add the remaining curry powder and warm it a minute, until the aroma lifts.
Add the tomatoes and chilli and reduce them to a thick base without loose liquid.
Pour in the coconut milk with the tamarind and warm it without letting it boil.
Return the fish to the sauce, let it sit five minutes and serve with rice and coriander.
ut-vitumbua: Drain the soaked rice and grind it with the coconut milk into a smooth, loose batter.
Stir in the yeast, sugar, cardamom, salt and grated coconut.
Leave the batter to ferment four hours in the warm, until it is covered in bubbles.
Stir the batter and check the body: it should pour in a ribbon rather than drop in a lump.
Heat the dimpled pan and brush each well with oil.
Fill the wells three-quarters full and cook three minutes, until the edges set.
Turn the cakes with a skewer and give them three minutes more, to a browned sphere.
ut-eru: Simmer the beef and tripe with the onion and a stock cube for an hour, until tender.
Soak the dried fish in hot water twenty minutes and flake it, taking out the bones.
Shred the eru leaf as fine as you can, rolling it tight before cutting.
Rinse the waterleaf and cut it coarsely; it wilts right down as it cooks anyway.
Put the waterleaf into the pot with the meat and let it wilt, giving up its juice.
Add the eru, fish, crayfish and chilli and stew twenty minutes with the lid on.
Pour in the palm oil, stir it through and cook ten minutes more uncovered.
ut-koki-corn: Soak the beans four hours, then rub them between your hands so the skins come away.
Rinse the beans several times, pouring off the floating skins, until the grains are clean and white.
Grind the beans with the onion and chilli into a thick paste, adding water a spoon at a time.
Beat the mass by hand or with a spatula for ten minutes, until it lightens and turns airy.
Warm the palm oil and work it into the mass to an even orange.
Pass the banana leaves over a flame until pliable and spoon the mass onto them with the greens.
Fold the parcels, tie them and steam them an hour and a half, until firm.
ut-kleftiko: Cut deep slits into the lamb and push a sliver of garlic into each.
Rub the meat with salt, pepper, oregano, olive oil and lemon juice.
Leave the lamb to marinate in the fridge for at least four hours.
Cut the potatoes into large wedges and lay them in the base of a clay dish.
Set the meat on the potatoes and add the bay, cinnamon and lemon halves.
Cover it and seal the join with a strip of dough or a double layer of foil.
Bake at 160 °C for five hours without opening it and rest it twenty minutes.
ut-koupepia: Scald the vine leaves for a minute and spread them on a cloth.
Mix both minces with the raw rice, grated onion, tomatoes and herbs.
Work in the cinnamon, mint, salt, pepper and half the olive oil.
Put a spoon of filling on a leaf, fold the sides in and roll it into a tight cylinder.
Line the pot with torn leaves so the rolls do not catch.
Pack the rolls in tight layers seam down and weight them with a plate.
Pour in water with lemon juice and oil and cook them an hour, covered, over a low heat.
ut-lampuki-pie: Fry the fish steaks three minutes a side and let them cool.
Lift the flesh off the bones, picking out every small bone.
Fry the onion, add the cauliflower florets and stew them ten minutes.
Add the spinach, tomato paste, olives, capers, sultanas and walnuts and cook it dry.
Cool the filling completely and fold the fish into it in pieces.
Line a tin with pastry, add the filling and cover it with a second sheet, crimping the edge.
Glaze it with egg, cut vents and bake at 190 °C for forty-five minutes, to a golden crust.
ut-lampuki-pie-gfnf: Fry the fish steaks three minutes a side and let them cool.
Lift the flesh off the bones, picking out every small bone.
Fry the onion, add the cauliflower florets and stew them ten minutes.
Add the spinach, tomato paste, olives, capers, sultanas and pumpkin seeds and cook it dry.
Cool the filling completely and fold the fish into it in pieces.
Line a tin with gluten-free pastry, add the filling and cover it with a second sheet, crimping the edge.
Glaze it with egg, cut vents and bake at 190 °C for forty-five minutes, to a golden crust.
ut-imqaret: Chop the dates and put them in a pan with the zests, aniseed and liqueur.
Cook the filling over a low heat for twenty minutes, to a thick even paste.
Cool the filling completely; warm, it tears the pastry as you wrap it.
Cut the margarine into the flour with salt to a crumb and bring the dough together with cold water.
Roll the dough into a long strip twelve centimetres wide.
Lay a rope of the date paste down the centre, fold the edges over and press the seam.
Cut it on the diagonal into diamonds and fry them at 180 °C, two minutes a side.
ut-imqaret-gf: Chop the dates and put them in a pan with the zests, aniseed and liqueur.
Cook the filling over a low heat for twenty minutes, to a thick even paste.
Cool the filling completely; warm, it tears the pastry as you wrap it.
Cut the margarine into the gluten-free flour with salt to a crumb and bring the dough together with cold water.
Roll the dough into a long strip twelve centimetres wide.
Lay a rope of the date paste down the centre, fold the edges over and press the seam.
Cut it on the diagonal into diamonds and fry them at 180 °C, two minutes a side.
ut-fergese: Char the peppers over a flame or under a grill until the skins blacken.
Put the hot peppers in a bag for ten minutes and peel them.
Soften the onion and garlic in butter and stir in a spoon of flour.
Add the chopped tomatoes and reduce them to a thick base with no loose liquid.
Cut the peeled peppers into strips and stir them into the tomato base.
Mash the curd cheese with the feta and work it into the hot mixture.
Transfer it to a clay pan and bake at 200 °C for twenty minutes, until it bubbles.
ut-fergese-gf: Char the peppers over a flame or under a grill until the skins blacken.
Put the hot peppers in a bag for ten minutes and peel them.
Soften the onion and garlic in butter and stir in a spoon of gluten-free flour.
Add the chopped tomatoes and reduce them to a thick base with no loose liquid.
Cut the peeled peppers into strips and stir them into the tomato base.
Mash the curd cheese with the feta and work it into the hot mixture.
Transfer it to a clay pan and bake at 200 °C for twenty minutes, until it bubbles.
ut-ballokume: Beat the softened butter with the sugar with a wooden spoon for twenty minutes, to a pale fluffy mass.
Add the yolks one at a time, still beating in the same direction.
Add the vanilla, salt and soda and beat five minutes more.
Work in the cornmeal a little at a time, to a firm but pliable dough.
Rest the dough fifteen minutes so the meal takes up the moisture.
Shape walnut-sized balls and set them well apart on parchment.
Bake at 170 °C for twenty minutes, to a pale gold edge, and cool them on the tray.
ut-sarmale-moldovenesti: Take the head apart into leaves and pare down the thick rib at the base of each.
Fry the onion in oil until golden and cool it completely.
Mix the mince with the raw rice, onion, dill, thyme, salt and pepper.
Halve the larger leaves and roll parcels the size of a thumb.
Line the base of a pot with leaf trimmings and pieces of smoked rib.
Pack the sarmale in tight circles, laying ribs between every other layer.
Pour over tomato juice and water, cover with torn leaves and stew at 150 °C for three hours.
ut-mucenici: Dissolve the yeast with a spoon of sugar in the warm milk and leave it to foam.
Knead a dough from the flour, sponge, eggs, sugar, zest, vanilla, salt and softened butter.
Let it rise somewhere warm for an hour and a quarter, until doubled.
Divide the dough into twelve and roll each into a forty-centimetre rope.
Twist each rope into a figure of eight, joining the ends, and set it on a tray.
Prove them thirty minutes and bake at 180 °C for twenty minutes, until golden.
Brush the hot mucenici with honey and cover them thickly with ground walnuts.
ut-kuurdak: Dice the tail fat and render it in a cauldron to golden crackling.
Lift out the crackling with a slotted spoon and set it aside; it goes back at the very end.
Cut the meat into walnut-sized pieces and fry it in batches to a dark crust.
Return all the meat to the pot, salt it, add the cumin and cover it for fifteen minutes.
Add the onion in thick half-moons and fry until it turns translucent.
Add the potatoes in large pieces and cook twenty minutes more, covered.
Return the crackling, add the garlic and coriander and serve it straight from the pot with gluten-free bread.
ut-boorsok: Dissolve the yeast with the sugar in the warm milk and leave it fifteen minutes, until it foams.
Knead a soft dough from the flour, sponge, egg, melted butter and salt.
Let it rise somewhere warm for an hour, until doubled.
Knock the dough back and roll it out to exactly a centimetre thick.
Cut it into four-centimetre diamonds and let them rest twenty minutes.
Heat the oil to 180 °C and lower the diamonds in in small batches.
Fry them a minute and a half a side, turning with a slotted spoon, to golden puffs.
ut-tushbera: Knead a stiff dough from the flour, egg, water and salt and work it fifteen minutes.
Cover the dough and rest it forty minutes; that is what makes it pliable.
Chop the lamb and tail fat by knife into a fine crumb.
Mix the meat with finely chopped onion, cumin, salt and pepper.
Roll the dough until translucent and cut five-centimetre rounds.
Fold the dumplings, sealing the edge and bringing two corners together into a ring.
Cook them in the boiling broth for eight minutes and serve them in a bowl with katyk and coriander.
ut-tushbera-gf: Knead a stiff dough from the gluten-free flour, egg, water and salt and work it fifteen minutes.
Cover the dough and rest it forty minutes; that is what makes it pliable.
Chop the lamb and tail fat by knife into a fine crumb.
Mix the meat with finely chopped onion, cumin, salt and pepper.
Roll the dough until translucent and cut five-centimetre rounds.
Fold the dumplings, sealing the edge and bringing two corners together into a ring.
Cook them in the boiling broth for eight minutes and serve them in a bowl with katyk and coriander.
ut-chakka: Line a colander with two layers of close-woven cloth and pour in the katyk.
Knot the corners of the cloth and hang the bundle over a bowl somewhere cold.
Leave it draining a full day, until the mass is as firm as soft curd.
Pound the garlic with a pinch of salt into a smooth paste.
Chop the coriander, dill, basil and spring onion as fine as you can.
Fold the herbs and garlic into the strained mass with a spatula, without mashing it.
Salt it, smooth it in a bowl, press a hollow with a spoon and pour the oil into it.
ut-khuushuur: Knead an unleavened dough from the flour, water and salt and work it ten minutes to smoothness.
Cover the dough and rest it thirty minutes.
Chop the lamb fine by knife, fat and all, and mix it with the onion and garlic.
Pour the broth into the filling and work it to a loose but not runny mass.
Divide the dough into balls and roll each into a twelve-centimetre round.
Put filling on one half, fold it over and crimp the edge tightly and evenly.
Fry them in a centimetre of oil, three minutes a side, to a blistered crust.
ut-khuushuur-gf: Knead an unleavened dough from the gluten-free flour, water and salt and work it ten minutes to smoothness.
Cover the dough and rest it thirty minutes.
Chop the lamb fine by knife, fat and all, and mix it with the onion and garlic.
Pour the broth into the filling and work it to a loose but not runny mass.
Divide the dough into balls and roll each into a twelve-centimetre round.
Put filling on one half, fold it over and crimp the edge tightly and evenly.
Fry them in a centimetre of oil, three minutes a side, to a blistered crust.
ut-suutei-tsai: Break up the brick tea and cover it with a litre of cold water in a pot.
Bring it to the boil and cook five minutes, until the liquor darkens.
Pour in the milk and bring it back to the boil, watching that it does not run over.
Salt it and cook five minutes more over a low heat.
Ladle the tea up and pour it back from a height a dozen times.
Add the butter and stir until it disappears.
Strain it into bowls and serve it hot, with toasted gluten-free flour if you like.
ut-ashak: Knead a dough from the flour, water and salt and rest it forty minutes under film.
Chop the spring onion very fine, salt it and wring it out in a cloth.
Fry the onion with the mince, add the tomato paste and stew it twenty minutes.
Whisk the yoghurt with crushed garlic and salt and leave it at room temperature.
Roll the dough thin and cut eight-centimetre rounds.
Add the leek filling, fold each into a half-moon and crimp the edge tight.
Boil the dumplings five minutes, lay them on the yoghurt, spoon the sauce over and dust with mint and chilli.
ut-ashak-gf: Knead a dough from the gluten-free flour, water and salt and rest it forty minutes under film.
Chop the spring onion very fine, salt it and wring it out in a cloth.
Fry the onion with the mince, add the tomato paste and stew it twenty minutes.
Whisk the yoghurt with crushed garlic and salt and leave it at room temperature.
Roll the dough thin and cut eight-centimetre rounds.
Add the leek filling, fold each into a half-moon and crimp the edge tight.
Boil the dumplings five minutes, lay them on the yoghurt, spoon the sauce over and dust with mint and chilli.
ut-bolani: Knead a soft dough from the flour, warm water, a spoon of oil and salt.
Cover the dough and rest it thirty minutes.
Boil the potatoes soft, drain them and mash them without milk.
Work the spring onion, coriander, chilli, salt and pepper into the mash.
Divide the dough into six and roll each into a thin round.
Spread the filling thinly over half the round and fold the other half over, pressing the edge.
Cook them on a brush-oiled pan, four minutes a side, until spotted.
ut-bolani-gf: Knead a soft dough from the gluten-free flour, warm water, a spoon of oil and salt.
Cover the dough and rest it thirty minutes.
Boil the potatoes soft, drain them and mash them without milk.
Work the spring onion, coriander, chilli, salt and pepper into the mash.
Divide the dough into six and roll each into a thin round.
Spread the filling thinly over half the round and fold the other half over, pressing the edge.
Cook them on a brush-oiled pan, four minutes a side, until spotted.
